run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-16T13:13:12Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The alert reports a nonzero request-error rate for frontend-proxy in otel-demo (0.0111). Observed evidence: frontend-proxy does emit error spans, and its access log shows repeated HTTP 503 responses with response flag 'UC upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination}', where the upstream is the frontend (e.g. 13:01:02, 13:02:16, 13:04:07, 13:11:59, 13:13:59, 13:18:05). Sampled traces of these 503s contain only the load-generator GET, the frontend-proxy 'ingress' span and its 'router frontend egress' child (http.status_code 0, error=true) - no frontend span - so the proxy's error rate before the alert start came from the frontend upstream terminating the connection before responding. A second, larger episode occurred at 13:16-13:17: frontend-proxy returned HTTP 500 (via_upstream) on /api/cart, /api/checkout and /api/cart reads from 13:15:46 to 13:16:14 and 503 UC at 13:16:59-13:17:00; in the same minute frontend-proxy logged 186 ingress and 186 egress error spans (error-span ratio ~0.07). That episode coincides exactly with a cart Deployment rollout restart: a new ReplicaSet cart-84889c965d was created at 13:15:42 with only the pod-template annotation kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt added (image/env/resources identical to cart-755465879b), the old pod was deleted at 13:15:45 and the new cart process only bound its port at 13:16:07. That rollout cannot explain the alert start at 13:13:12; it is a later, separate contributor. The alert's exact expression and its 0.0111 value could not be reproduced from the visible trace metrics, and the RequestErrorRate rule is not present in this Prometheus. Frontend-proxy's own pod is ready, restartCount 0 and only ~8% CPU-throttled, so the errors originate in its frontend upstream, not in the proxy binary itself; the precise frontend-side mechanism remains unproven (frontend container logs could not be read).

claims.text: At 13:34:00, frontend-proxy error spans counted over 20m were: span_name 'ingress' status_code ERROR 108.35, span_name 'router frontend egress' ERROR 97.83, alongside STATUS_CODE_UNSET 9060.75 ('ingress') and 9070.22 ('router frontend egress').

In the 24h range view the frontend-proxy error series first returns a point at 12:59:24 (increase over 5m: 'ingress' 33.33) and stays small (0-5.56 per 5m) until a distinct spike in the 5m bucket ending 13:19:24: 'ingress' 108.89 and 'router frontend egress' 103.33; frontend 'grpc.oteldemo.CartService/AddItem' 57.78, 'grpc.oteldemo.CartService/GetCart' 25.56, 'grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder' 20 and 'executing api route (pages) /api/cart' 83.33 also peak in that same bucket.

Per-minute error spans show the spike is confined to the minute ending 13:17:00: frontend-proxy 'ingress' 186 and 'router frontend egress' 186, frontend 'POST' 140, 'executing api route (pages) /api/cart' 108.6, 'grpc.oteldemo.CartService/AddItem' 71.8, 'GET /api/cart' 36.9, frontend 'tcp.connect' 14; neighbouring minutes carry only 0-6 errors, and ingress errors are 0 in 13:07-13:16 except 2 at 13:15.
The frontend-proxy error-span ratio (error spans / all spans, 2m increase) is 0-0.0011 for 12:57 through 13:16 and 13:19-13:26, and rises to 0.0702 at 13:17:00 and 0.0699 at 13:18:00.

A tag search returned 9 sampled traces whose frontend-proxy 'ingress' spans carry status tags error=true, http.status_code=503, otel.status_code=ERROR, starting between 12:54:14 and 13:01:03; each sampled trace also has a load-generator 'GET' span with http.status_code=503 and a frontend-proxy 'router frontend egress' span with error="true" and http.status_code="0".

Whole trace c40b3222b9a63859e138ddf42bd9991a contains exactly 4 spans: load-generator 'user_get_recommendations' (no status), load-generator 'GET' (http.status_code 503, otel.status_code ERROR), frontend-proxy 'ingress' (error=true, http.status_code 503, ERROR) and its child frontend-proxy 'router frontend egress' (error="true", http.status_code="0"); there is no frontend span in the trace.

frontend-proxy access logs between 13:00:00 and 13:15:00 contain 7 responses with status 5xx, all of the form '"GET /api/... HTTP/1.1" 503 UC upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination} ... frontend 100.96.3.80:8080 ...' with 0 response bytes and durations 423-788ms, timestamped 13:01:02.509, 13:02:16.801, 13:02:16.972, 13:04:07.516, 13:04:19.080, 13:11:59.251 and 13:13:59.245; the upstream is named 'frontend'.

frontend-proxy access logs between 13:14:00 and 13:20:00 contain the same 503 UC upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination} pattern against upstream 'frontend', e.g. 'GET /api/products/2ZYFJ3GM2N ... 503 UC ... 349ms' at 13:18:05.557.

frontend-proxy access logs between 13:15:00 and 13:18:00 show HTTP 500 '- via_upstream' with upstream 'frontend' on 'POST /api/cart', 'GET /api/cart' and 'POST /api/checkout' from 13:15:46.371 to 13:16:14.343 (small 21-byte error bodies), followed by 503 UC upstream_reset_before_response_started for 'GET /api/products/...' at 13:16:59.717, 13:16:59.962 and 13:17:00.006.

The cart Deployment was rolled out at 13:15:42: ReplicaSet cart-84889c965d was created at 13:15:42 and holds 1 ready replica, while ReplicaSet cart-755465879b (created 12:44:32) was scaled to 0; events record 'Scaled up replica set cart-84889c965d from 0 to 1' and 'SuccessfulCreate' at 13:15:42, 'Killing/Stopping container cart' on pod cart-755465879b-rh5r4 and 'SuccessfulDelete' at 13:15:45, and 'Started container cart' on cart-84889c965d-tkxdz at 13:15:44.

The two cart ReplicaSet pod templates are identical in image (ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-cart), environment (CART_PORT 8080, VALKEY_ADDR valkey-cart:6379, FLAGD_HOST flagd, OTLP endpoint), and resources (cpu 45m/mem 165Mi limits); the only difference is the new ReplicaSet template annotation kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-16T13:15:42Z.

Pod cart-84889c965d-tkxdz reports restartCount 0, no lastState and container started 13:15:44, and its cart container log records 'Overriding HTTP_PORTS ... Binding to values defined by URLS instead' at 13:16:07.911 - i.e. the new cart process was still initialising about 25s after the old pod was deleted.

Of the 21 otel-demo pods, all except cart started 12:44:32-12:46:27; the only pod younger than the incident is cart-84889c965d-tkxdz (startTime 2026-11-16T13:15:42Z). frontend-675fd7b5c5-64mj8 (ready, restartCount 0, started 12:44:34) and frontend-proxy-6b4d584985-v4lvt (ready, restartCount 0, started 12:44:37) were not restarted.

Resource limits are frontend cpu 100m / memory 200Mi and frontend-proxy cpu 30m / memory 50Mi; measured CPU throttling of frontend cgroup periods is 0.33-0.41 continuously from 12:55 to 13:31, while frontend-proxy throttling is 0.07-0.13, and frontend RSS is 221-234 MiB throughout the window versus its 200Mi limit (frontend-proxy RSS ~36 MiB).
At query time the cart, frontend and frontend-proxy Deployments each report replicas 1, readyReplicas 1, availableReplicas 1 with Available=True (MinimumReplicasAvailable).

The fraud-detection container of pod fraud-detection-9fb7d885b-v48vh was OOMKilled with exitCode 137, finishedAt 13:21:12 and restarted (startedAt 13:21:13, restartCount 1); events show container Created/Started again at 13:21:13.

frontend-proxy's own pod is not failing on its own resources: container restartCount 0, RSS ~36 MiB against a 50Mi limit, CPU throttling only 0.07-0.13, and its recorded error spans are on the 'router frontend egress' client span to the frontend (http.status_code 0, error=true) whose parent is the 'ingress' span - i.e. the failures are caused by the upstream frontend, not by the proxy process.

The error rate that the alert reports for frontend-proxy, and which is visible before 13:13:12, is produced by the frontend upstream closing/terminating the proxy-to-frontend connection before sending response headers (response flag 'upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination}', egress span http.status_code 0, no frontend span in the trace), so the proxy answers 503. The frontend-side reason for those resets is not established from the available evidence.

The separate 13:16-13:17 error spike was caused by the cart Deployment rollout restart at 13:15:42: cart stopped serving when the old pod was deleted at 13:15:45 and its replacement only bound its port at 13:16:07, so the frontend returned HTTP 500 for /api/cart and /api/checkout, which frontend-proxy relayed and which produced 186 ingress and 186 egress error spans in that minute. This episode starts 2.5 minutes after the alert timestamp and therefore cannot explain the alert's 13:13:12 start.

Chronic pressure on the frontend container (CPU throttling ~0.33-0.41 of periods against a 100m limit and RSS ~221-234 MiB against a 200Mi limit, constant from 12:55 to 13:31) may make the frontend slow enough to drop or reset some in-flight proxy requests, contributing to the recurring 503 UC errors. The evidence shows the condition is constant across the window, so it does not by itself explain why the alert started at 13:13:12.

The fraud-detection container OOM (OOMKilled exitCode 137 at 13:21:12, restart 13:21:13) is not a cause of this alert: it happened after the alert start (13:13:12) and after the 13:16-13:17 error peak, and the only fraud-detection error spans in the 20m view are 'flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream' ~1.05 and ResolveInt 0, with no evidence tying fraud-detection to frontend-proxy's 503/500 responses whose logged upstream is 'frontend'.

Read the frontend container's stdout/stderr (and its previous instance) for 12:54-13:20 and correlate the 503 UC timestamps (13:01:02, 13:02:16, 13:04:07/19, 13:11:59, 13:13:59, 13:16:59, 13:18:05) with frontend app errors/GC pauses; the frontend pod's logs were not readable in this Run, so this is the missing evidence needed to confirm why it terminates proxy connections before responding.

Review the frontend container sizing (cpu limit 100m, memory limit 200Mi versus observed ~0.11 core usage, 33-41% throttling and ~221-234 MiB RSS) and consider raising the CPU/memory limits or reducing the load-generator rate, since sustained throttling/memory pressure is a plausible contributor to dropped responses.

Treat cart restarts as error-generating events: the kubectl rollout restart at 13:15:42 removed the only cart replica before its replacement was serving (port bound at 13:16:07), producing 500s on /api/cart and /api/checkout. A rolling replacement with more than one replica or a readiness gate on the new cart pod would avoid this error burst.
